Formulation:
Predisposing: Female sex; family history of migraine.  
Precipitating: Recent work-related stress; prolonged screen exposure.  
Perpetuating: Inadequate analgesic dosing; photophobia limiting activities; concern about possible “genetic” migraine increases vigilance.  
Protective: Supportive household; health-seeking behaviour; intact coping skills.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem (Recurrent severe headache / probable migraine):
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve effective pain relief; prevent future severe episodes; identify triggers.  
- Clinical Goal(s): Confirm migraine diagnosis; optimise acute treatment; consider prophylaxis if frequency increases; monitor psychosocial impact.  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Use prescribed analgesia as directed (e.g., Naproxen ± Paracetamol/Codeine).  
  • Keep a detailed headache diary (timing, severity, triggers, response to medication).  
  • Reduce screen brightness, take regular breaks, maintain hydration.  
  • Return for review in 1–2 weeks or sooner if worsening or neurological symptoms develop.  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Provide prescription for appropriate NSAID ± combination analgesic.  
  • Educate on correct dosing of Ibuprofen/Naproxen and safe use of Codeine.  
  • Review headache diary at follow-up; consider migraine prophylaxis if ≥4 disabling days/month.  
  • Arrange eye test referral if visual strain persists.  
  • Provide safety-net advice regarding red-flag symptoms (vision loss, weakness, thunderclap onset).

Secondary Problem (Mild situational work-related stress):
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain work performance without exacerbating headaches; manage stress.  
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor for emergence of anxiety/mood symptoms; encourage stress-management strategies.  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Employ brief mindfulness or relaxation breaks during work.  
  • Maintain regular sleep and hydration.  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Re-assess stress and mental health symptoms at review; offer psychological strategies or referral if indicated.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Migraine nature, analgesic dosing, trigger identification, red-flag symptoms.  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating pain, new focal neurological deficits, persistent visual changes, lack of response to medication.  
- Coping Strategies: Scheduled breaks from screen, hydration, stress-reduction techniques, headache diary.

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)  
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded  
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None at present  
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable  
- Review Date: 1–2 weeks (or sooner if deterioration)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine (with possible aura): High likelihood – unilateral eye-predominant pain, photophobia, visual scintillations, nausea, family history.  
- Tension-type headache: Medium likelihood – diffuse dull pain, work stress, prolonged computer use.  
- Acute sinusitis (frontal/ethmoid): Low–Medium likelihood – periorbital pain, gradual onset; lacks nasal/fever features.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Formal mood screen, sleep/appetite details, vital signs, neurological exam findings, emergency contact details, GP information.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality notes: Consultation focused on headache; minimal mental health content; no overt psychiatric symptoms discussed.
